statement: Fix 0 < T < 1, a minimizer γ, and u, a as above. For an integer N ≥ 1 put ∆ = T/N and tj = j∆. On independent standard normal variables Z1, . . . , ZN+1, define Y0 = 0, Yj = Yj−1 + √ ∆Zj + ∆γ(tj−1)u(tj−1, Yj−1), 1 ≤ j ≤ N, (7.2) cj = (︁ Ea(tj−1, Yj−1)2)︁−1/2 > 0, gj = cja(tj−1, Yj−1)Zj. (7.3) For all sufficiently large N these constants are finite and positive. For these mesh counts, let FG denote the standard normal distribution function and set FN = sgn (︁ u(T, YN ) + 2FG(ZN+1) − 1 )︁ , Aj = E[FN gj], Bi = E[FN Zi], A0 = 0. Here 1 ≤ j ≤ N and 1 ≤ i ≤ N + 1 in the definitions of Aj and Bi. The value of the sign at zero is immaterial. Then lim N→∞ N ∑︂ j=0 AjBj+1 = ∫︂ T 0 Ea(t, Xt) dt. (7.4) Letting T ↑ 1 on the right gives P∗.
